title: The exchange morphisms on the truncation triangles form a morphism of exact couples
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$. On the bounded below derived categories of etale abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] put
$$
 \Phi=g^{-1}\circ Rf_*,\qquad \Psi=Rf'_*\circ g'^{-1}:\ \Dplus(X_{\Et})\longrightarrow\Dplus(Y'_{\Et}),
$$
with $u^{-1}$ the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and $Ru_*$ the derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and let $\xi_L:\Phi(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi(L)[1]$, $\zeta_L:\Psi(L[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Psi(L)[1]$ be the composite shift-commutation isomorphisms (for $u^{-1}$ the identity of termwise shifted complexes, for $Ru_*$ the isomorphism $\sigma$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]). Let $\Ex_\square:\Phi\to\Psi$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ and, for $q\in\mathbf Z$, let
$$
 T_q:\quad \tau_{\leq q-1}K\xrightarrow{\,i_q\,}\tau_{\leq q}K\xrightarrow{\,j_q\,}\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\xrightarrow{\,k_q\,}(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]
$$
be the truncation triangle [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], $\mathcal H^n$ denoting cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For $F\in\{\Phi,\Psi\}$, with $c_F=\xi$ resp. $\zeta$, define bigraded etale sheaves on $Y'$ and maps
$$
 D_F^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F\tau_{\leq q}K),\qquad E_F^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),
$$
$$
 \alpha_F=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F i_{q+1}):D_F^{p,q}\to D_F^{p-1,q+1},\qquad g_F=\mathcal H^{p+q}(F j_q):D_F^{p,q}\to E_F^{p,q},
$$
$$
 f_F:E_F^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{p+q}(c_{F,\tau_{\leq q-1}K}\circ F k_q)}\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl((F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]\bigr)=\mathcal H^{p+q+1}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)=D_F^{p+2,q-1},
$$
and put $t_D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K}):D_\Phi^{p,q}\to D_\Psi^{p,q}$ and $t_E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}):E_\Phi^{p,q}\to E_\Psi^{p,q}$.

Then:

(1) for $F=\Phi$ and $F=\Psi$, $(D_F,E_F,\alpha_F,f_F,g_F)$ is an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple];

(2) $(t_D,t_E)$ is a morphism of exact couples from the $\Phi$-couple to the $\Psi$-couple: $t_D\circ\alpha_\Phi=\alpha_\Psi\circ t_D$, $t_E\circ g_\Phi=g_\Psi\circ t_D$ and $t_D^{p+2,q-1}\circ f_\Phi=f_\Psi\circ t_E^{p,q}$ in every bidegree;

(3) for every $(p,q)$, under the canonical isomorphisms $E_\Phi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Phi\,\mathcal H^q(K))=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)$ and $E_\Psi^{p,q}\cong\mathcal H^p(\Psi\,\mathcal H^q(K))=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ (given by $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ of the iterated shift isomorphisms $\xi^{(-q)},\zeta^{(-q)}$, the identity $\mathcal H^{p+q}(L[-q])=\mathcal H^p(L)$, and $\mathcal H^p\circ g^{-1}=g^{-1}\circ\mathcal H^p$), the map $t_E^{p,q}$ is the degree-$p$ exchange map of the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$,
$$
 \mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)}):\ g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\longrightarrow R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K).
$$

proof.text: **Step 1 (the image triangles are distinguished).** $T_q$ is a distinguished triangle of $D(X_{\Et})$ with terms in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. The functors $g^{-1}$ and $g'^{-1}$ are triangulated with the identity as shift isomorphism, being induced by the exact sheaf functors applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; $Rf_*$ and $Rf'_*$ are triangulated with shift isomorphism $\sigma$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. A composite of triangulated functors, with the composite shift isomorphism, is triangulated (if $GT$ is distinguished with third map $\sigma^G\circ G(w)$, then $HGT$ has third map $H(\sigma^G)$-composed, $\sigma^H_{G}\circ H(\sigma^G)\circ HG(w)$, which is the composite shift isomorphism applied to $HG(w)$). Hence for $F\in\{\Phi,\Psi\}$ the triangle $F(T_q)=(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K,F\tau_{\leq q}K,F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]),Fi_q,Fj_q,c_{F}\circ Fk_q)$ is distinguished in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$.

**Step 2 (claim (1): exact couples).** Apply the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the distinguished triangle $F(T_q)$ of Step 1: with $n=p+q$ it reads
$$
 \cdots\to\mathcal H^{n}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Fi_q)}\mathcal H^n(F\tau_{\leq q}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^n(Fj_q)}\mathcal H^n(F(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]))\xrightarrow{\delta^n}\mathcal H^{n+1}(F\tau_{\leq q-1}K)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^{n+1}(Fi_q)}\cdots,
$$
where the connecting map $\delta^n$ is $\mathcal H^n$ of the third map $c_F\circ Fk_q$ followed by $\mathcal H^n(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$. In the notation of the statement these maps are $\alpha_F:D_F^{p+1,q-1}\to D_F^{p,q}$, $g_F:D_F^{p,q}\to E_F^{p,q}$, $f_F:E_F^{p,q}\to D_F^{p+2,q-1}$ and $\alpha_F:D_F^{p+2,q-1}\to D_F^{p+1,q}$. Consecutive composites vanish and exactness at the three spots is exactly $\ker\alpha=\operatorname{im}f$, $\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$, $\ker g=\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of [def-sp-exact-couple] in bidegree $(p,q)$ (the first one read at $D^{p+2,q-1}$ after renaming). As $p,q$ are arbitrary, both couples are exact couples. (This is the argument of [lem-sp-truncation-couple-exact] with $Rv$ replaced by the triangulated functor $F$.)

proof.text:
**Step 3 (the exchange morphisms form a morphism of triangles).** By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (2), applied to the triangle $T_q$ (whose shift isomorphisms $\xi,\zeta$ are those used here), the triple $(\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q-1}K},\Ex_{\square,\tau_{\leq q}K},\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]})$ is a morphism of triangles $\Phi(T_q)\to\Psi(T_q)$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]:
$$
 \Psi i_q\circ\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}=\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q}K}\circ\Phi i_q,\qquad \Psi j_q\circ\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q}K}=\Ex_{\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}\circ\Phi j_q,
$$
$$
 \zeta\circ\Psi k_q\circ\Ex_{\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]}=\Ex_{\tau_{\leq q-1}K}[1]\circ\xi\circ\Phi k_q .
$$
The first two squares are the naturality of $\Ex_\square$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; the third is naturality for $k_q$ followed by the compatibility of $\Ex_\square$ with the shift, part (1) of that lemma.

proof.text: **Step 4 (claim (2): a morphism of exact couples).** Apply $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ to the three squares of Step 3. The first square for $T_{q+1}$ gives $t_D^{p-1,q+1}\circ\alpha_\Phi=\alpha_\Psi\circ t_D^{p,q}$; the second for $T_q$ gives $t_E^{p,q}\circ g_\Phi=g_\Psi\circ t_D^{p,q}$; the third, together with the naturality of the identification $\mathcal H^{n}(M[1])=\mathcal H^{n+1}(M)$ (which carries $\mathcal H^n(a[1])$ to $\mathcal H^{n+1}(a)$), gives $t_D^{p+2,q-1}\circ f_\Phi=f_\Psi\circ t_E^{p,q}$. These are the three compatibilities of a morphism of exact couples. (Equivalently: the connecting maps of the long exact sequences of Step 2 are natural for morphisms of triangles, Mathlib `Functor.homologySequenceδ_naturality`.)

source.place: Section 12.21 (exact couples, Definition 011Q); the morphism is that of Lemma 0DDE's spectral sequences, etale-cohomology.tex line 18708

proof.text: **Step 5 (claim (3): the first graded component).** Let $M=\mathcal H^q(K)$, a sheaf placed in degree $0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (1) with $n=-q$, $\zeta^{(-q)}_M\circ\Ex_{\square,M[-q]}=\Ex_{\square,M}[-q]\circ\xi^{(-q)}_M$. Applying $\mathcal H^{p+q}$ and the identity $\mathcal H^{p+q}(L[-q])=\mathcal H^p(L)$ (natural in $L$), $t_E^{p,q}$ corresponds to $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,M}):\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*M)\to\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}M)$. Finally $\mathcal H^p(g^{-1}Rf_*M)=g^{-1}\mathcal H^p(Rf_*M)=g^{-1}R^pf_*M$, because $g^{-1}$ on $\Dplus$ is the exact sheaf functor applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] and an exact functor commutes with the cohomology of a complex, and $\mathcal H^p(Rf'_*g'^{-1}M)=R^pf'_*(g'^{-1}M)$ by the definition of $R^pf'_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. So $t_E^{p,q}$ is the degree-$p$ exchange map $g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\to R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ of the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(K)$, the map of Stacks' $E_2$-pages.
